_comment: Approver-role registry for the /cmemail readiness gate. Version-controlled (NOT gitignored) so the gate behaves identically for everyone on the team -- this is change-process policy, not per-user state. The gate reads a PR's approved reviews (github.com or git.innova-partners.com) and checks that an APPROVED review exists from each role the tier requires. GitHub exposes only user.login, so matching is by login. A required role with no login that can be matched is treated as NOT satisfied (the gate blocks and says so) -- it never silently passes. The gate only verifies approvals that actually land in the source (PR reviews / STCM fields); approvals obtained some other way (see vpApproval below) are deliberately out of scope and must never be added as a gate condition.

em.name: Owen Winkler
em.role: EM and Director (one person holds both; an APPROVED review from Owen is the EM/Director sign-off)

roles.director: same person as em (Owen Winkler); do not require separately -- the 'em' check already covers the Director authority

tierRequiredRoles._comment: Which approver roles the gate must find an APPROVED review from, per requested tier. 'peer' = any APPROVED review from someone who is neither the PR author nor the 'em' on this list (GitHub won't let an author approve their own PR, so a peer is always distinct). 'em' is Owen, whose single approval is the combined EM/Director sign-off, so Director is never gated separately. VP approval is never gated (see vpApproval).

vpApproval._comment: VP sign-off exists in the change process but is obtained THROUGH the generated email, not in the PR or Jira: the VP is a recipient who approves by reply. Its absence from the source is expected and must NEVER be a gate condition -- do not add a 'vp' role to tierRequiredRoles. Recorded here only so the VP is included as an email recipient for the tiers that require VP sign-off.
vpApproval.name: Todd
vpApproval.note: Last name / address intentionally left for the requester to fill on the Cc line; confirm before hardcoding.
